# AI solution lens 0.4.0

The criteria a design adds when any of its elements uses a model to produce its output: a generative or predictive model, a retrieval pipeline, a judge, a guard. They do not replace the core lens; they ask what changes when part of the design is non-deterministic, learned from data, priced per call and supplied by someone else. Each criterion reads the ai facet of the elements that carry one.

Applies to designs with the `ai-solution` profile. Source: [`standards/assessment/lenses/ai-solution.yaml`](../../standards/assessment/lenses/ai-solution.yaml).

## FIT: Fitness for AI

Is a model the right tool, and is its role in the design bounded?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AIS-FIT-01](ais-fit-01.md) | Does the design say why a model is needed, and what a deterministic alternative would cost? | major | reviewer |
| [AIS-FIT-02](ais-fit-02.md) | Is the model's role in each element stated, and limited to that role? | minor | both |

## MOD: Model and value chain

Is the model a pinned, documented, replaceable dependency?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AIS-MOD-01](ais-mod-01.md) | Is every model version pinned, with a documented route to change it? | major | tool |
| [AIS-MOD-02](ais-mod-02.md) | Is there a model card or system card for every model, and an AI bill of materials for the design? | minor | both |
| [AIS-MOD-03](ais-mod-03.md) | Can the model or its provider be replaced, and is there a fallback model or path? | major | both |

## EVAL: Evaluation as evidence

Do evals prove the design meets its quality scenarios, with each kind of error costed and measured on enough cases, and do they gate release?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AIS-EVAL-01](ais-eval-01.md) | Does every model-backed element have evals with a metric and a threshold? | blocker | tool |
| [AIS-EVAL-02](ais-eval-02.md) | Does at least one offline eval gate release? | major | tool |
| [AIS-EVAL-03](ais-eval-03.md) | Do the evals cover the design's quality scenarios, its risk scenarios and the populations it serves? | major | reviewer |
| [AIS-EVAL-04](ais-eval-04.md) | Is every LLM-as-judge eval calibrated against human labels? | major | tool |
| [AIS-EVAL-05](ais-eval-05.md) | Has the design been red-teamed against the OWASP LLM risks that apply to it? | major | both |
| [AIS-EVAL-06](ais-eval-06.md) | Does each eval that classifies (retrieval, answer or abstain, routing, a guard) name its positive class and set a separate threshold on false positives and on false negatives, weighted by what each error costs, rather than relying on F1 or accuracy alone? | major | both |
| [AIS-EVAL-07](ais-eval-07.md) | Is abstention evaluated, with questions the sources cannot answer in the test set, and the rate of answering them bounded? | major | both |
| [AIS-EVAL-08](ais-eval-08.md) | Is permission trimming tested as people with different access, with zero tolerance for content a user may not read? | major | tool |
| [AIS-EVAL-09](ais-eval-09.md) | Is each threshold backed by enough test cases to tell a pass from chance, with the interval reported? | major | reviewer |
| [AIS-EVAL-10](ais-eval-10.md) | Are the evals repeatable evidence, run more than once on a versioned, held-out set? | major | tool |

## DATA: Grounding and data

Is the data the model sees owned, permissioned, current and traceable?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AIS-DATA-01](ais-data-01.md) | Is every grounding source a named, owned and classified data set? | major | tool |
| [AIS-DATA-02](ais-data-02.md) | Is retrieval trimmed to what the caller may see? | blocker | tool |
| [AIS-DATA-03](ais-data-03.md) | Are data provenance, freshness and drift monitored? | minor | both |
| [AIS-DATA-04](ais-data-04.md) | Is data used for training, fine-tuning or evaluation licensed and permitted for that use? | major | reviewer |

## IO: Inputs and outputs

Is untrusted input contained and model output validated before it does anything?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AIS-IO-01](ais-io-01.md) | Is every model that receives untrusted input identified, with its untrusted inputs named? | major | tool |
| [AIS-IO-02](ais-io-02.md) | Is model output constrained and validated before it reaches a tool, a store, a query, code or a user? | blocker | tool |
| [AIS-IO-03](ais-io-03.md) | Does the design avoid relying on the system prompt for security, or on keeping it secret? | major | reviewer |

## OPS: Running AI

Is the model observed, bounded in cost and latency, and able to fail safely?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AIS-OPS-01](ais-ops-01.md) | Are token, rate, cost and time limits set on every model call? | major | tool |
| [AIS-OPS-02](ais-ops-02.md) | Are model calls traced with prompts, outputs, tokens and cost, to the GenAI conventions? | minor | both |
| [AIS-OPS-03](ais-ops-03.md) | Is there a latency and quality budget per scenario, with a degraded mode when it is missed? | minor | reviewer |

## HUM: People and obligations

Is human oversight designed, users told, and the regulatory class known?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AIS-HUM-01](ais-hum-01.md) | Is the level of human oversight stated for each model-backed decision, and proportionate to its impact? | major | both |
| [AIS-HUM-02](ais-hum-02.md) | Are users told when they deal with AI or receive generated content? | major | both |
| [AIS-HUM-03](ais-hum-03.md) | Is the design's class under the AI regulations that apply to it recorded, with the impact assessment it requires? | major | both |
